requirements.title: Authorized public repository
requirements.acceptance: Real URL, verified owner, new repository and checked public access.

requirements.title: License and notices
requirements.acceptance: Selected license published; dependency notices and provenance reviewed.

requirements.title: Honest English origin story
requirements.acceptance: English README explains the long-held idea and AI assistance without invented facts; the prior EN/FR requirement is superseded.

requirements.title: Actual implementation status
requirements.acceptance: Roadmap and compatibility link to evidence; no fake badges or unimplemented capabilities presented as available.

requirements.title: Clean publication
requirements.acceptance: Explicit staging, content review and secret scan; no private material published.

requirements.title: Contribution and security
requirements.acceptance: English CONTRIBUTING, SECURITY, conduct rules and decisions are accessible.

requirements.title: Non-destructive inventory
requirements.acceptance: Private report and sanitized summary; actual versions and architecture verified.

requirements.title: Idempotent setup
requirements.acceptance: Tested shell/PowerShell scripts with diagnostics; no Python required.

requirements.title: Windows x64 installation
requirements.acceptance: Actual Windows user build/run/test and VSIX workflow verified.

requirements.title: Linux x64 installation
requirements.acceptance: Actual Linux user build/run/test and VSIX workflow verified.

requirements.title: macOS arm64 installation
requirements.acceptance: Actual macOS user build/run/test and VSIX workflow verified.

requirements.title: Transparent prerequisites
requirements.acceptance: Manifest separates seed tools, OS/SDK, runtime, packaging and optional dependencies.

requirements.title: No required Python
requirements.acceptance: Install, compile, execute and normally test NAJA without Python.

requirements.title: No hidden Python runtime
requirements.acceptance: Audit binary imports, processes, dependencies and distribution for CPython/PyPy/MicroPython.

requirements.title: No required Python oracle
requirements.acceptance: Normal test suite is independent, using specification and metamorphic cases.

requirements.title: No user AI account
requirements.acceptance: Compile and execute offline without a Claude/OpenAI account or AI API.

requirements.title: No Python editor dependency
requirements.acceptance: LSP, DAP and VSIX do not require Pyright/Pylance or the Python extension.

requirements.title: Versioned reference baseline
requirements.acceptance: Inventory the target grammar, edition, date, hash and productions.

requirements.title: Complete target grammar parsing
requirements.acceptance: Every pinned grammar production has positive and negative tests.

requirements.title: Separate compatibility dimensions
requirements.acceptance: Assess parsing, semantics, library coverage and ABI independently.

requirements.title: Explicit unsupported features
requirements.acceptance: Recognized but unimplemented executable constructs produce diagnostics, never fabricated results.

requirements.title: Preserved standard source forms
requirements.acceptance: Unmodified .py corpus; project aliases disabled for the standard dialect by default.

requirements.title: Block depth
requirements.acceptance: Correct root/sibling/nested levels with precise errors and suggested fixes.

requirements.title: Clauses and suites
requirements.acceptance: Test if/else, try/except/finally, match/case, def/class, with/async and multiline forms.

requirements.title: Same-line suite ambiguity
requirements.acceptance: if flag:(0) without an indented suite preserves its standard meaning.

requirements.title: No blind replacement
requirements.acceptance: Preserve strings, comments, slices, attributes and nested expressions.

requirements.title: Six comparison aliases
requirements.acceptance: All six requested comparisons support aliases and canonical forms.

requirements.title: Precedence and comparison chains
requirements.acceptance: Preserve observable behavior and single evaluation of intermediate operands.

requirements.title: Hygienic builtin aliases
requirements.acceptance: Document and test scope resolution and shadowing.

requirements.title: Safe local alias manifest
requirements.acceptance: Declarative TOML; reject conflicts/duplicates; package scope and cache invalidation verified.

requirements.title: CST and source maps
requirements.acceptance: Exact diagnostics, formatting and debugging positions after normalization.

requirements.title: Values and numbers
requirements.acceptance: Working None/bool/arbitrary hosted int/float/str/bytes with tested errors.

requirements.title: Collections
requirements.acceptance: Lists, tuples, ordered dictionaries and sets with declared mutation, identity and exception behavior.

requirements.title: Functions and closures
requirements.acceptance: Execute keyword/default arguments, lambdas, closures and decorators.

requirements.title: Objects
requirements.acceptance: HATCH classes, inheritance and methods with positive and negative tests.

requirements.title: Control and patterns
requirements.acceptance: Execute scoped conditions, loops, comparisons and pattern matching.

requirements.title: Errors and resources
requirements.acceptance: Exceptions, finally and context managers preserve required cleanup.

requirements.title: Iteration
requirements.acceptance: Execute the supported iterator, generator and comprehension contracts.

requirements.title: Asynchrony
requirements.acceptance: Async/await and networking tasks include cancellation and resource bounds.

requirements.title: Imports and modules
requirements.acceptance: Deterministic resolution, declared cycle handling and useful errors.

requirements.title: Semantics before speed
requirements.acceptance: Arithmetic, evaluation-order and floating-point tests detect invalid optimizations.

requirements.title: Basic CLI
requirements.acceptance: version/help/doctor/init/check/build/run/test return reliable results and exit codes.

requirements.title: Formatting
requirements.acceptance: Idempotent fmt with explicit alias/marker options and no semantic changes.

requirements.title: Documentation and packages
requirements.acceptance: Working doc/package, manifests/lockfiles and tested offline use.

requirements.title: I/O and serialization
requirements.acceptance: Independent file/Unicode path/JSON/TOML services needed by the tools.

requirements.title: Native runtime
requirements.acceptance: Memory, object and error services implemented in the independent NAJA distribution.

requirements.title: Deterministic builds
requirements.acceptance: Versioned caches, invalidation and reproducible parameters documented and tested.

requirements.title: Actual code generation
requirements.acceptance: Functions, branches, calls, structures and memory compile to machine code.

requirements.title: Independent backend
requirements.acceptance: Linux x86-64 requires neither LLVM nor C/Rust translation.

requirements.title: Independent linking
requirements.acceptance: NAJA build-closure symbols, relocations and ELF handled without a required external linker.

requirements.title: Decoupled backend
requirements.acceptance: IR/APIs do not freeze LLVM/Rust internals; optional adapter is isolated.

requirements.title: ABI and diagnostics
requirements.acceptance: Calling conventions, intrinsics and unsupported-target cases are checked.

requirements.title: Self-hosted sources
requirements.acceptance: Compiler and required runtime/tool closure are NAJA sources or documented target primitives.

requirements.title: B1 B2 B3 stages
requirements.acceptance: Actually perform rebuilding with complete manifests and logs.

requirements.title: No mandatory original seed
requirements.acceptance: B2/B3 neither execute nor load the Rust seed or derived opaque blobs.

requirements.title: Isolated reconstruction
requirements.acceptance: Reference-target build without Python/Rust/Cargo/LLVM/external C compiler or network.

requirements.title: Fixed-point comparison
requirements.acceptance: Compare unsigned artifacts, explain differences and never arbitrarily exclude code.

requirements.title: Evolution in NAJA
requirements.acceptance: Implement, compile and test a real compiler change in NAJA without changing B0.

requirements.title: Traceable chain
requirements.acceptance: Explicit seed, source, versions and allowed OS dependencies.

requirements.title: Distinct capability profiles
requirements.acceptance: hosted/core/embedded enforce capabilities without imposing a full hosted runtime.

requirements.title: CPU discovery
requirements.acceptance: Count and architecture have documented visible-logical-processor semantics.

requirements.title: Instruction objects
requirements.acceptance: Typed machine blocks check registers/clobbers/ABI; verify output and disassembly.

requirements.title: Permissions
requirements.acceptance: CPU objects grant no privileges or arbitrary register access; negative cases tested.

requirements.title: Freestanding execution
requirements.acceptance: Run an OS-independent program on a documented QEMU target with observable output.

requirements.title: FFI and memory
requirements.acceptance: Ownership, alignment, lifetime and bounds contracts tested.

requirements.title: Two-line TCP
requirements.acceptance: Actual native echo using the contractual example on all product targets.

requirements.title: Two-line HTTP
requirements.acceptance: Valid HTTP response through the contractual example and a real browser/native client.

requirements.title: Events
requirements.acceptance: Receive/error decorators and API work; bind errors propagate.

requirements.title: Streams and framing
requirements.acceptance: Test fragmentation/coalescence, bounded framing and chunk/message distinction.

requirements.title: Limits and backpressure
requirements.acceptance: Handle slow clients, bounded buffers/connections and partial writes.

requirements.title: Lifecycle
requirements.acceptance: Cancellation, peer closure and graceful shutdown leave no owned orphan resources.

requirements.title: Network safety
requirements.acceptance: Loopback default, no automatic firewall change, strict bounded HTTP parsing.

requirements.title: Installable VSIX
requirements.acceptance: Clean-profile installation, artifact hash and verified toolchain detection.

requirements.title: Visual language support
requirements.acceptance: Correct highlighting, indentation, folding, comments and bracket pairs.

requirements.title: Semantic LSP
requirements.acceptance: Diagnostics, completion, hover/signatures and symbols use the real frontend.

requirements.title: Navigation
requirements.acceptance: Safe multi-file definition/reference lookup and rename.

requirements.title: Markers and aliases
requirements.acceptance: Correct fixes, completion, manifest navigation and inlay hints.

requirements.title: Project build and run
requirements.acceptance: Create/select target/build/run workflows produce actual results.

requirements.title: Test Explorer
requirements.acceptance: Discover/run/cancel tests; failures remain visible failures.

requirements.title: Native debugging
requirements.acceptance: Real program breakpoints/steps/stack/variables/stop with source maps.

requirements.title: Workspace Trust
requirements.acceptance: No project-code execution on opening an untrusted workspace.

requirements.title: Host and targets
requirements.acceptance: Correct binary selection; no global .py takeover; remote limits documented.

requirements.title: Usability and docs
requirements.acceptance: English commands/help/logs and accessibility; no forced telemetry or separate user Node install.

requirements.title: Extension contracts
requirements.acceptance: Versioned schemas/capabilities without compulsory LLVM/Rust internals.

requirements.title: Numerical library
requirements.acceptance: Additional native CPU example written in NAJA without parser changes.

requirements.title: Quantum library
requirements.acceptance: Small bounded local NAJA simulator clearly distinguished from real QPU execution.

requirements.title: Durability
requirements.acceptance: Compatibility/migration tests across multiple consumers independent of core internals.

requirements.title: Negative memory tests
requirements.acceptance: Bounds, lifetimes, cycles, errors and resources tested under claimed guarantees.

requirements.title: Concurrency
requirements.acceptance: Shared access/cancellation tested; guarantees and limitations published.

requirements.title: Fuzzing and regression tests
requirements.acceptance: Parser/manifest/protocol corpora; reproducible crashes and regression coverage.

requirements.title: Protected CI
requirements.acceptance: Least privilege, pinned actions, protected secrets and substantive actual checks.

requirements.title: Independent audit
requirements.acceptance: Adversarial review or explicit self-review; blocking defects fixed.

requirements.title: Honest benchmarks
requirements.acceptance: Publish versions, machines, flags, repetitions, comparable workloads and limits.

requirements.title: User documentation
requirements.acceptance: English tested quickstart, limitations, contributor/bootstrap/resume guidance.

requirements.title: Release artifacts
requirements.acceptance: Per-target archives, VSIX, sources, manifests, checksums and notices.

requirements.title: Traceable acceptance
requirements.acceptance: Every mandatory gate links to release commit and evidence; no hidden skips.

requirements.title: Usable handoff
requirements.acceptance: Actual state, HANDOFF and RESUME maintained; no unexecuted background-work promises.

requirements.title: Full independent Python semantics
requirements.acceptance: Separately tracked future objective; no support claim before implementation and evidence.

requirements.title: Full independent Python standard library
requirements.acceptance: Separately tracked future objective; no support claim before implementation and evidence.

requirements.title: Python packages and CPython ABI without CPython runtime
requirements.acceptance: Separately tracked future objective; no support claim before implementation and evidence.

requirements.title: Browser WebAssembly and DOM backend
requirements.acceptance: Separately tracked future objective; no support claim before implementation and evidence.

requirements.title: GPU/MLIR and complete AI training
requirements.acceptance: Separately tracked future objective; no support claim before implementation and evidence.

requirements.title: Drivers and a complete operating system
requirements.acceptance: Separately tracked future objective; no support claim before implementation and evidence.

requirements.title: Real QPU access and QIR compilation
requirements.acceptance: Separately tracked future objective; no support claim before implementation and evidence.

requirements.title: I3 autonomy on every architecture and OS
requirements.acceptance: Separately tracked future objective; no support claim before implementation and evidence.

requirements.title: Complete cells and selections
requirements.acceptance: Complete top-level expression/sequence; # %% outside strings; reject selections that remove required context or parent conditions.

requirements.title: Independent native execution
requirements.acceptance: Compile and load machine-code fragments without a hidden interpreter; Python/Jupyter/LLVM are not required.

requirements.title: Coherent persistent state
requirements.acceptance: Module bindings/imports/values/globals persist under NAJA semantics and remain isolated across sessions.

requirements.title: Explicit order and effects
requirements.acceptance: One execution per action, no hidden replay or removed parent conditions; Run All follows source order.

requirements.title: Safe versions and invalidation
requirements.acceptance: Old function references remain valid; type/global assumptions stay correct; live code is retained and memory limits published.

requirements.title: Non-destructive compilation failure
requirements.acceptance: Parse/type/link in candidate state; pre-execution failure leaves committed bindings and user initializers untouched.

requirements.title: Honest execution failure
requirements.acceptance: Report possible partial state/external effects; no general rollback promise.

requirements.title: Interruption and lifecycle
requirements.acceptance: Dedicated worker, bounded output, stop/reset, stale-generation invalidation and declared owned-resource limitations.

requirements.title: Real trust and security boundaries
requirements.acceptance: Workspace Trust, no automatic launch or effectful inspection, private history; process separation is not claimed as a sandbox.

requirements.title: Controlled cache and loading
requirements.acceptance: Complete cache keys, integrity/permissions, dependency invalidation and preserved OS memory protections; no persisted raw pointers.

requirements.title: Versioned protocol and sources
requirements.acceptance: Request/session/generation/cell IDs, dialect/alias/source maps, framed output and stale-message rejection.

requirements.title: Native interactive CLI
requirements.acceptance: REPL, stdio service and cell commands work/documented without editor or Python.

requirements.title: VS Code cells
requirements.acceptance: Real Run Cell/Selection/All, stop/reset, bounded output/state, stale markers and export, without Python extension.

requirements.title: Export and explicit replay
requirements.acceptance: Export source without private memory/output, explicit ordering, fresh validation and no implicit historical execution.

requirements.title: Verified cross-platform sessions
requirements.acceptance: Actually test hosted Windows x64/Linux x64/macOS arm64 sessions; publish OS limits and excluded targets.

requirements.title: Self-hosted session
requirements.acceptance: Cell compiler, loader, session runtime/protocol/cache belong to the independent Linux x86-64 NAJA closure.

requirements.title: No imposed interactive AOT overhead
requirements.acceptance: Audit linked artifacts for absence of unused controllers/tables/history; deterministic comparison with component present/absent.

requirements.title: Separate timing costs
requirements.acceptance: Publish compile/load, warm native compute, editor exchange and cold total; separate final-release measurements.

requirements.title: Measured AOT non-regression
requirements.acceptance: Capture baseline before integration; predeclare method/budgets and repeat measures; significant regression blocks R17 unless explicitly addressed.

requirements.title: Session-independent release
requirements.acceptance: Build only declared sources/inputs, never memory/history; session activity must not alter identical-input artifacts.

requirements.title: English specifications and prompts
requirements.acceptance: All official documents, instructions, prompts, roadmap and task/requirement narratives are English; no mandatory bilingual duplicate remains.

requirements.title: English tools and diagnostics
requirements.acceptance: Generated CLI help/errors, stable diagnostic messages and VS Code labels/settings are English and exercised in real tool tests.

requirements.title: English source-facing material
requirements.acceptance: Official API names, comments/docstrings and examples are English while Unicode data and user-defined aliases remain supported.

requirements.title: Non-destructive translation migration
requirements.acceptance: Preserve existing IDs, technical intent, code/history/status/evidence; record expanded-contract revalidation without erasing prior proofs.

requirements.title: Audited language coverage
requirements.acceptance: Commit-linked English review covers tracked/generated surfaces and narrowly documented legal/data/raw-evidence exceptions.

requirements.title: English public collaboration
requirements.acceptance: Public README/story, contribution/security guides, issue/PR templates and release notes are accurate and English.

requirements.title: Per-case 100-to-25 code target
requirements.acceptance: Each DX01–DX06 NAJA normalized task footprint is <=25% of both equivalent idiomatic Rust and C++ baselines; no averaging or silent waiver.

requirements.title: Fair executable baselines
requirements.acceptance: Both baselines actually pass shared behavior tests, use reviewed idiomatic libraries and are pinned without artificial verbosity.

requirements.title: Complete source accounting
requirements.acceptance: Count all task-owned source/helpers/configuration/macros/DSL inputs/shims; disclose generated output and library costs with a file ledger.

requirements.title: Readable normalized counting
requirements.acceptance: Pinned readable formatters and preregistered counting rules prevent brace, packing, chained-operation or hidden-code score manipulation.

requirements.title: Concise genuine microkernel
requirements.acceptance: DX01 actually boots the declared freestanding QEMU target, reports memory, handles timer ticks and halts with explicit support assumptions.

requirements.title: Productive native applications
requirements.acceptance: DX02–DX04 networking/HTTP/CLI library workflows preserve equivalent validation, lifecycle, errors, bounds and output.

requirements.title: Native CSV aggregation
requirements.acceptance: DX05 uses an independent schema-aware CSV pipeline with bounded groups, deterministic sums/output and tested malformed/oversized input.

requirements.title: Native JSONL transformation
requirements.acceptance: DX06 streams validated JSONL to deterministic CSV with declared error, memory, cancellation and output-commit behavior.

requirements.title: General reusable libraries
requirements.acceptance: Short APIs are public, versioned, independently tested and reusable across inputs; report implementation/maintenance/dependency/unsafe costs separately.

requirements.title: Independent library closure
requirements.acceptance: Productivity libraries introduce no Python or mandatory foreign-runtime/service shortcut and remain compatible with self-hosted/core capability rules.

requirements.title: Behavior and safety parity
requirements.acceptance: Shared positive/negative tests prove equivalent features, validation, numeric semantics, resource cleanup and safety assumptions.

requirements.title: Resource and runtime budgets
requirements.acceptance: Predeclare and test relevant execution/latency/memory/binary/compile budgets; a brevity win cannot override a failed correctness or resource gate.

requirements.title: Measured creation-time reduction
requirements.acceptance: Controlled matched sessions show lower median time to accepted initial solutions against both baselines under the preregistered uncertainty rule; missing/inconclusive data is not a pass.

requirements.title: Measured change-time reduction
requirements.acceptance: Run matched change requests, report active/wall/compile/review time and experience; label human versus AI-assisted populations, with no inference from LOC alone.

requirements.title: Preregistered reproducible evidence
requirements.acceptance: Publish case/rule hashes, exact source/versions/inputs, raw per-case counts/times/resources and failed outcomes; unmeasured values stay null/not_run.

requirements.title: Discoverable productive APIs
requirements.acceptance: English guides/templates and real semantic VS Code completion expose high-level APIs plus explicit low-level controls without new required syntax.
